summary: This paper compares two fabricated electrode materials: a citric-acid-crosslinked polyaniline conducting polymer hydrogel (CPH) cathode and LiF/HCl-etched Ti3C2Tx MXene anode. The CPH delivered the highest individual-electrode gravimetric capacitance, 402.5 F/g at 1 A/g in 1 M H2SO4, whereas Ti3C2Tx delivered 213.8 F/g under −0.35–0.3 V versus SCE. They were combined into a CPH//Ti3C2Tx asymmetric supercapacitor with 90.3 mF/cm2 at 1 mA/cm2 and 16.6 μWh/cm2 at 0.6 mW/cm2. Film thicknesses, MXene loading, BET areas, pore sizes, and printed interlayer d-spacings were not reported.
